resources.string: Without HTTPS, your username and app password can be read by anyone on the network between this phone and the server. Only use this on a network you trust.
Actua forgets the server address, app password and backup password on this phone. Backups already on the server are not deleted.
Backups are encrypted on this phone with your backup password before they leave it. The server only ever receives an encrypted file.
Enter the username and app password.
Enter the full WebDAV address, starting with https://.
This address uses plain HTTP. Use https://, or turn on Allow unencrypted HTTP if you trust the network.
The backup folder can only be a simple path such as Actua Backups.
The server rejected the username or app password, or this account may not use that folder.
The server could not find the address or folder. Check the address.
The server has no room for the backup. Free some space and try again.
The server\'s certificate could not be verified.
The server redirected to another address. Use the address it redirects to, usually the https:// one.
This server does not support renaming files, which Actua needs to upload safely.
The server did not keep the whole backup, so it was removed. Try again.
Could not reach the server. Check the address and your connection.
After each automatic backup, Actua uploads the newest one when the phone has a connection, and tries again if it fails. The last error shows here.
The backup password is not set, so nothing was uploaded.
Backup created and queued for WebDAV upload.
Backup created and queued for Google Drive and WebDAV upload.
No Actua backups were found in the WebDAV folder.
Actua needs the “Nearby devices” permission to reach a server on your home network. Allow it in Android Settings → Apps → Actua → Permissions, then try again.
